source_name: Ministry of Digital Transformation portal — Macedonian translations of EC Country Reports
why_relevant: Official Macedonian-language versions of the EC country reports; useful for extracting the exact local terminology used for EU financial-services concepts (glossary building) and for tracking how the government renders EU requirements domestically.

source_name: Central Financing and Contracting Department (CFCD), MK Ministry of Finance — Twinning & IPA
why_relevant: CFCD contracts IPA/Twinning projects in MK; its twinning pages and tender notices reveal which financial-sector directives are being transposed next (the twinning fiche names the acquis and beneficiary institution years before the law appears).

source_name: MK Ministry of Finance — EU projects / twinning news (e.g. Solvency II insurance harmonisation twinning)
why_relevant: Beneficiary-side reporting on twinning projects that write MK financial legislation (e.g. transposing Solvency II into the Law on Insurance); indicates which EU member-state administration is the partner and what the deliverable law is.

source_name: EEAS — EU Delegation to North Macedonia
why_relevant: The Delegation publishes twinning project announcements and vacancy/fiche details (e.g. MK18 IPA FI 01 19 on budget planning and internal control), Growth Plan disbursement news, and EU-funded financial-sector assistance — an early indicator of upcoming regulatory work.

source_name: Reform and Growth Facility — North Macedonia Reform Agenda and payment-condition documents
why_relevant: The Reform Agenda ties EUR ~750m of disbursements to dated, verifiable reform steps (2024-2027), several in the financial/digital/business-environment area; these are the hardest deadlines in MK's regulatory calendar because money depends on them.

source_name: Sobranie (MK Parliament) — legislative harmonisation / 'European flag' bills
why_relevant: Bills flagged with the EU flag (европско знаменце) travel under the shortened harmonisation procedure; the parliamentary pipeline shows which EU-aligning financial laws are actually about to pass and when, complete with the declaration of conformity (изјава за усогласеност) referencing the source directive.

source_name: Insurance Supervision Agency (АСО) — Fintech strategy for financial regulators 2023-2027
why_relevant: Joint strategy of the MK financial regulators (NBRM, ASO, SEC, MoF) setting the fintech/regulatory agenda that is explicitly benchmarked against EU acts; identifies planned regulatory interventions and cross-regulator coordination bodies. NOTE: URL captured from search results and may contain a transcription error — resolve from aso.mk before relying on it.

source_name: Deutsche Bundesbank — international central bank dialogue / twinning newsletter
why_relevant: EU member-state central banks act as twinning partners to the National Bank of North Macedonia; their newsletters describe the technical content and timing of alignment projects (e.g. a 'twinning light' project with North Macedonia) that domestic sources report only sparsely.

source_name: European Parliament — Western Balkans / North Macedonia annual resolutions and fact sheets
why_relevant: The EP's annual report on North Macedonia and the OEIL procedure files add political pressure points and sometimes name specific financial-sector shortcomings; useful as a second, independent EU-side read on alignment pace.

source_name: World Bank — Western Balkans SEPA/payments analytical features
why_relevant: IFI commentary that quantifies the practical effect of MK's PSD2/SEPA alignment and often reveals remaining implementation gaps (pricing, PSP licensing, instant payments) not stated in official EU texts.

source_name: European Policy Institute Skopje (ЕПИ) — shadow reports on negotiating chapters
why_relevant: Civil-society shadow reports track chapter-by-chapter alignment independently of government claims and are published in Macedonian and English; they surface implementation gaps and are a rich pointer to actors and terminology. Currently confirmed for Chapter 23 — coverage of Cluster 3/Chapter 9 needs checking.

source_name: Local Macedonian media EU-report coverage (Meta.mk, Sloboda Evropa MK, Nova Makedonija, MKD.mk)
why_relevant: Fast local-language signal of what MK institutions say about EC findings (e.g. NBRM claiming high alignment in monetary policy per the EC report) and of EU-flagged laws entering parliament; useful for timing and for actor/terminology discovery, not for authoritative facts.

source_name: Licentium — North Macedonia payments/e-money licensing hub
why_relevant: Commercial licensing-intelligence page summarising the MK Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (Official Gazette No. 90/2022, in force 1 Jan 2023) as a PSD2/EMD2/PAD/IFR transposition, with licensing categories — a fast English-language bridge from EU directive to MK legal citation.

source_name: TAIEX (EC Technical Assistance and Information Exchange) — event/expert-mission database
why_relevant: TAIEX missions are a leading indicator of where the Commission thinks MK institutions are weak: a July 2026 TAIEX mission in Skopje examined the independence of the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia, an issue that typically precedes legislative change to the central bank law.

source_name: КИБС — Правила за работа (clearing house operating rulebook PDF)
why_relevant: The operating rulebook is the binding contract-level regulation for participants: admission/participation criteria, cut-off times, settlement cycles, obligations and sanctions. This is de-facto payments regulation not published in the Official Gazette.

source_name: НБРСМ — Македонски интербанкарски платен систем (МИПС) page
why_relevant: MIPS is the central bank owned/operated RTGS; this page is the anchor for its legal basis, participant set, dual-currency (MKD/EUR) operation and links to rules and technical characteristics.

source_name: НБРСМ — Правила за работа на МИПС (versions index)
why_relevant: Versioned archive of the MIPS operating rules — the single best place to detect rule amendments, effective dates and compliance deadlines imposed on RTGS participants (e.g. amendment no. 02-21254/1 of 14.06.2022).

source_name: НБРСМ — Технички карактеристики на МИПС
why_relevant: Technical specification layer of the RTGS (message standard 'Стандард за намена и формат на пораките во МИПС', interfaces). Changes here signal mandatory participant-side technical migrations (e.g. ISO 20022).

source_name: НБРСМ — Шема на платни системи и системи за порамнување на хартии од вредност
why_relevant: Authoritative map of every designated payment and securities settlement system in the country — the definitive actor list for this cell (MIPS, KIBS, CaSys, CSD) and the entry point to each operator.

source_name: НБРСМ — Рамка за обелоденување и методологија за проценка на ПИФП (oversight assessment framework, PDF)
why_relevant: PFMI-based disclosure and assessment methodology the central bank applies to KIBS/CaSys/MIPS. Drives the operators' own disclosure frameworks and remediation obligations, which in turn become participant-facing rule changes.

source_name: НБРСМ — Интернационален картичен систем АД Скопје (КаСис) oversight page
why_relevant: Central bank page describing CaSys as an operated/overseen card payment system — the authoritative statement of CaSys's status, participants and role as the domestic card processing/clearing rule-setter.

source_name: НБРСМ — КИБС profile page (regulator's view of the clearing house)
why_relevant: Regulator-published description of KIBS as MDNS operator for retail payments, its ownership, participant categories (banks, treasury, health fund) and oversight status — useful to cross-check KIBS's own claims.

source_name: CaSys International (Интернационален картичен систем АД Скопје) — corporate site & LinkedIn
why_relevant: The domestic card processor/personalisation bureau and card-system operator; its product and compliance announcements (EMV, 3-D Secure, tokenisation, scheme mandates) set technical requirements for issuing/acquiring banks and merchants.

source_name: OneID (КИБС e-identification / qualified trust service)
why_relevant: KIBS's eIDAS-aligned e-ID and qualified trust service — the identity/authentication rail that payment participants must integrate for SCA and onboarding. Its certification and policy documents are quasi-binding technical rules.

source_name: Македонска банкарска асоцијација (MBA) — e-Bulletin
why_relevant: The banking association's bulletin carries interviews with KIBS management (e.g. April 2026 e-Bulletin with GM Goran Anastasovski) and industry commentary that reveals scheme roadmaps, instant-payment milestones and participant readiness before official rule publication.
